title: ws_rate_limiting plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `ws_rate_limiting` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component WsRateLimitingConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

WsRateLimitingConfig.description:
Configuration for the `ws_rate_limiting` plugin. Enforces WebSocket
frame rate limiting using a token-bucket algorithm, per connection by
default or as an aggregate budget shared by every session of one
consumer, client IP, or proxy (`limit_by`). When the bucket is
exhausted, the plugin sends a WebSocket close frame (RFC 6455 close code
1008 — Policy Violation) to both client and backend. Both directions
(client→backend and backend→client) consume from the same bucket. Both
values stay within 1–1000000. With `sync_mode: "redis"`,
`frames_per_second` and `burst_size` must also form an integer-multiple
refill window of at most 3600 seconds so Redis two-window enforcement
cannot over-admit or under-admit relative to the local token bucket,
including across Redis failure/recovery; a local-only policy accepts any
capacity/refill pair. Redis mode externalizes those per-connection
counters under a per-plugin/gateway-instance key namespace; it does not
coordinate a portable per-connection frame budget across gateway
instances, reconnects, or plugin rebuilds. Aggregate `limit_by` budgets
are keyed by their portable identity instead, so replicas of one policy
share them. `sync_mode` is parsed case-insensitively (`LOCAL`, `Redis`);
`redis` requires `redis_url`. Unknown top-level keys are rejected by the
runtime and by this schema. Counter storage supports only local memory
and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally unsupported.
Residual admission rules this schema cannot express, enforced by the
constructor alone: with `sync_mode: "redis"`, `burst_size` must be >=
`frames_per_second`, an integer multiple of it, and
`burst_size / frames_per_second` must be at most 3600 seconds.

frames_per_second.description: Token refill rate per second. Range 1–1000000. Must be greater than zero — configs with `frames_per_second: 0` are rejected at config load time. With `sync_mode: redis`, together with `burst_size`, must yield an integer-multiple refill window of at most 3600 seconds so Redis and local sustained rates match.

burst_size.description: Maximum burst capacity (tokens). Range 1–1000000. Defaults to the value of `frames_per_second` when not explicitly set. Must be greater than zero. With `sync_mode: redis` it must also be greater than or equal to `frames_per_second`, an integer multiple of `frames_per_second`, and yield a refill window (`burst_size / frames_per_second`) of at most 3600 seconds: configs that Redis cannot represent without over-admitting or under-admitting relative to the local token bucket are rejected at config load time. A local-only policy accepts any pair, including a burst smaller than the sustained rate.

close_reason.description: Close-frame reason text sent when the frame rate is exceeded. Truncated on a UTF-8 char boundary to 123 bytes (the RFC 6455 §5.5 control-frame payload limit) so the frame stays well-formed.

limit_by.description: Budget dimension. `connection` (default) gives every WebSocket session its own bucket. `consumer` shares one bucket across every session of the authenticated principal (a mapped Consumer, or an unmapped external identity keyed together with its verifying realm, so the two never share a bucket); anonymous sessions share their client IP's bucket. `ip` shares one bucket per resolved client IP. `service` shares one bucket per proxy. The identity is resolved once at upgrade admission. Aggregate budgets use the same 50,000-key local cap; with `sync_mode: redis` they are keyed by that identity (no per-instance UUID), so replicas of one policy share them.

sync_mode.description: Frame counter storage: 'local' (in-memory) or 'redis' (externalized per-connection counters namespaced per plugin/gateway instance; not a portable cross-instance budget), parsed case-insensitively. `redis` additionally requires `redis_url`. With an aggregate `limit_by` (`consumer`, `ip`, `service`) the Redis counter is keyed by that identity and shared by every replica of the policy; a refused frame batch is handed back, so refusals never consume the shared budget. Database-backed counters are unsupported. Any RESP-compatible server works.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL (e.g., redis://host:6379/0), required with sync_mode=redis. The database selector is a canonical decimal integer from 0 through 2147483647, without signs, zero-padding, or extra slashes. An absent path or bare slash selects database 0. Ferrum uses the portable signed-32-bit bound; redis-rs represents indexes as i64. The server separately checks its configured databases on SELECT. TCP port range is constructor-validated. URL fragments are forbidden; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share the surrounding key namespace. Must be non-empty when set. In the default `limit_by: connection` mode this plugin still prepends a per-instance UUID to every logical connection key, so an explicit shared prefix does not opt two plugin or gateway instances into a shared per-connection frame budget. Aggregate `limit_by` keys carry no instance UUID.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed closes the WebSocket with a policy Close frame; local_fallback explicitly opts into per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.
